content:
maya: Quick sync — we need to lock the rerank API surface for the next sprint. Major points: input shapes, top_k semantics, score normalization, and truncation behavior. Who can take notes?

kevin: I can. Can we list the customer asks that pushed this?

maya: Yeah — two enterprise search customers asked for: 1) stable top_k behavior across model upgrades; 2) predictable latency/cost for large candidate sets (10-50k); 3) ability to get both raw model scores and a normalized score for UI sorting.

sophia: For normalization, recommending we return both raw_score and normalized_score. Normalized_score should be in [0,1] using softmax over the returned candidates (not the whole corpus) unless user opts into global normalization. That keeps math simple and explains UI mapping.

kevin: Softmax over returned candidates is cheap only if we score them all server-side. For huge candidate sets customers will stream buckets; we need a policy for partial results. Suggest we accept candidate streams but normalization flag must be "per_batch" or "global". Default = "per_batch".

support_jordan: Customer note: some clients precompute embeddings and do dot-product on client — they want a simple top_k param where top_k=0 means "return all scores". Also they expect ties to preserve original order.

maya: Decisions we should make now: 1) input format (single query + list of candidates vs batch queries); 2) top_k semantics (k or 0); 3) score fields; 4) truncation/validation rules for very long candidates.

kevin: Proposal: input schema accepts either: (A) query + candidates[] (strings or {id, text, metadata}) or (B) queries[] with candidates[] for pairwise. top_k: integer >=0, where 0 => return all (with pagination). We should cap server-side max_candidates_per_request (configurable, default 50k) and return 413 if exceeded.

maya: Agree on schema A/B. For pagination when top_k=0, return a cursor token for next page. We need clear SLA notes for large jobs (async).

sophia: On scoring types, expose param score_type: ["prob", "logit", "cosine", "dot"]. For generative rerank (LM-based reranking), raw_score = logit or logprob; normalized_score = softmax(normed_logits). For embedding-based rerank, raw_score = dot/cosine. Normalized_score still derived using per-response softmax unless user asks for min-max scaling.

kevin: Implementation note: for embeddings we already have batched matrix multiply kernels — those scale. For LM-based we should early-terminate token generation for candidate scoring with prefix caching. Might need a separate internal route for heavy scoring to avoid latency SLO violations.

support_jordan: Truncation: Customers asked that we not silently truncate content. If a candidate exceeds token_limit, return 400 with field "candidate_too_long" that lists ids and max_allowed. Offer a truncate=true param to accept automatic truncation (with a warning flag in the response).

maya: Good — default should be strict (error) to avoid silent data loss. Truncate=true opt-in is fine. Also include a warning metadata field when truncate was applied.

sophia: Edge case: identical scores -> stable_sort by original index then by id. We should document tie-breaking. Also document floating point precision differences across model versions.

kevin: For top_k behavior: return top_k best candidates sorted by normalized_score desc. If top_k < returned_count (i.e., ties at the cutoff), include all tied candidates or use stable cutoff? I vote stable cutoff (deterministic) and a param include_ties=true to expand. Default false to keep bounded response size.

maya: So defaults: include_ties=false, normalization=per_batch softmax, top_k behavior deterministic cutoff, token_limit enforced error by default, truncate opt-in, return raw_score + normalized_score, accept id/text/metadata.

support_jordan: +1. Add an example response in docs showing both scores and a pagination cursor.

product-bot: Reminder: RFC doc skeleton created: /docs/rerank-api/spec-draft-1769501123. Meeting scheduled Thursday 11am to finalize launch criteria.

maya: I'll draft the launch criteria: end-to-end latency targets for 10/100/1k candidate sets, cost guidance per 1k candidates, and compatibility matrix (embedding vs LM rerank). I'll post a PR.

kevin: I'll prototype a sample request shape and perf numbers by Wed.

sophia: I'll add normalization math and recommended defaults to the RFC.

support_jordan: I'll add customer ask notes + a checklist for migration guidance (ties, truncation).

maya: Thanks all. Quick action items: kevin (prototype), sophia (math + examples), jordan (customer notes), maya (launch criteria + PR). We'll review Thursday. :thumbsup:
